_about: Layout v4 (New York Countdown, iteration 1: doc 14's ten holes), proposal by Claude 27 Nov 2026, not decided. Generated by tools/make_layout_nyc_v4.py on geometry v2 plus the 20 Nov room facts (console x 49-53, side exits). Positions are about +-0.5 m: they sit on values that are not measured. Hole local frames: see W/BRIEF.md; 'exit' is the page-frame local (u, v) where players leave for the next hole. footprints['scenery'] are standing scenery for walk-mode collisions. Scenery: position (x, z), rotation in degrees from +X toward +Z (the direction of the item's length), size [length, height, depth].

holes.name: Brownstone Stoops
holes.play: Stand beside the open tee side and putt along the top landing. The ball drops onto a stoop that sags toward the façade, over a skewed lip, then onto the green, and runs at the cup in a painted cellar hatch. A soft putt stalls on a terrace and is played on from there.
holes.mech: Lane 0.95 m on four boxes, each lower than the last: tee landing (1.0 m), T2 65 mm down (1.2 m, 1.5° cross-fall toward the façade), T3 20 mm down (1.0 m, lip skewed 20°), green 40 mm down (1.9 m). Cup 1.2 m past the last lip, 0.2 m off centre away from the sag. Ace about 2.4–2.5 m/s.
holes.build: Four terrace boxes on the factory deck with rounded lips and PVC angle nosings, one stepped rail, back corners filled. Brownstone-painted risers, iron-railing silhouettes, glow tape on every nosing, green LED. Shares the brownstone façade (lit windows, fire escape) with hole 9.
holes.miss: A short ball rests on a terrace within 0.5 m of a rail, so it is always in reach, and nothing rolls back up a step. A drop adds no speed, so the pace stays in the player's hands.
holes.risks: Chipped lips; players stepping onto terraces (boxes rated to stand on); the sag read as a build fault (paint a crack); the tee landing, about 225 mm off the floor, is high for small kids (junior tee on T2).
holes.clock: A window clock on the façade reads 11:59.
holes.surface: Green carpet grass on four terraces; brownstone risers with stone-look nosings.
holes.prop: Four terrace boxes on the factory deck with rounded lips and PVC angle nosings, one stepped rail, back corners filled. Brownstone-painted risers, iron-railing silhouettes, glow tape on every nosing, green LED. Shares the brownstone façade (lit windows, fire escape) with hole 9.
holes.robust: A short ball rests on a terrace within 0.5 m of a rail, so it is always in reach, and nothing rolls back up a step. A drop adds no speed, so the pace stays in the player's hands.

holes.name: Brooklyn Pizza
holes.play: One shot each, curling style. Putt down the lane, up the crust and onto a 1.6 m pizza. The ball's centre scores: centre pepperoni (the cup) 1, inner circle 2, on the pizza 3, anywhere else 4. Balls stay until all four have putted, so knock-ons count; the youngest player calls close ones.
holes.mech: Lane 2.6 m, 0.95 m wide, flaring to 1.75 m. The crust is a full-width 1:5 bevel rising 75 mm onto a house levelled to ±2 mm: eight Ø150 pepperoni, the centre one the flush cup, 3.8 m from the tee, inside a Ø0.60 m dashed circle. Ace about 2.3 m/s; the 2-point window is about ±4% of speed.
holes.build: A lane and a raised house deck, the crust bevel, flare walls, and an oven gutter behind the pizza: 120 mm wide, 45 mm deep, falling 3° to an open 250 mm pick-up pocket at one rail. Painted pizza, a 1.2 m slice sign, the pizzeria shopfront on the shared façade, "1 SHOT · CURLING" on the totem, orange LED.
holes.miss: Too soft rolls back down the crust and scores 4. Too hard drops into the oven gutter, scores 4 and can't come back, so smashing never pays. Nothing to clear between players.
holes.risks: Speed of the pizza surface (speed strip on 3 Dec); seams in the pizza; floor flatness under the levelled house; kids asking for another go.
holes.surface: Green carpet grass lane; a pizza painted on one carpet (cheese, pepperoni, crust ring).
holes.prop: A lane and a raised house deck, the crust bevel, flare walls, and an oven gutter behind the pizza: 120 mm wide, 45 mm deep, falling 3° to an open 250 mm pick-up pocket at one rail. Painted pizza, a 1.2 m slice sign, the pizzeria shopfront on the shared façade, "1 SHOT · CURLING" on the totem, orange LED.
holes.robust: Too soft rolls back down the crust and scores 4. Too hard drops into the oven gutter, scores 4 and can't come back, so smashing never pays. Nothing to clear between players.

holes.name: Hot Dog Cart
holes.play: Putt under the cart's arch between the ketchup and mustard bottles, up a short kerb and into an open giant bun whose curved faces steer the ball along a mustard squiggle to the cup near its closed end. Too soft rolls back off the kerb; too hard rebounds off the rounded end. The friendly ace hole and the food photo.
holes.mech: Lane 1.3 m. Cart arch 430 mm high, full width, counter 0.6 m deep. A 1:5 kerb rises 75 mm into the bun: halves 1.3 m long and 150 mm high, mouth 0.90 m narrowing to a 0.40 m channel, closed end R 0.20 m, cup 0.30 m from the end. Ace about 2.2–2.4 m/s.
holes.build: Bun boxes skinned in bent 3 mm hardboard, 5 mm EVA on the inner faces, PVC angle on the mouth noses, filled to the rails; the cart counter and arch as a flat. Golden bun, Ø180 bottles touching the rails, fries, a striped umbrella on a sandbagged post outside the rail, red LED.
holes.miss: Short rolls back off the kerb; wide stays in the lane; under the counter is at most 0.3 m in. Every ball ends within putter reach.
holes.risks: Mouth corners (PVC angle, 45° fills where they meet the rails); the cup must be dead flush; if aces pass about 40%, move the cup 0.1 m off axis.
holes.surface: Green carpet grass lane; a mustard squiggle painted inside the bun.
holes.prop: Bun boxes skinned in bent 3 mm hardboard, 5 mm EVA on the inner faces, PVC angle on the mouth noses, filled to the rails; the cart counter and arch as a flat. Golden bun, Ø180 bottles touching the rails, fries, a striped umbrella on a sandbagged post outside the rail, red LED.
holes.robust: Short rolls back off the kerb; wide stays in the lane; under the counter is at most 0.3 m in. Every ball ends within putter reach.

holes.name: Brooklyn Bridge
holes.play: One pair at each end of a narrow bridge with a hump and the cup on top. On "3-2-1" both putt at once. Too soft rolls back; too hard crosses to the other borough and is played by its owner from that end. Then the second pair. Groups with small kids take turns.
holes.mech: Lane 5.0 m, D-shaped end rails. A 0.60 m plateau 150 mm up with the cup in the middle; 12° ramps about 0.95 m long; approaches about 1.25 m. Rails narrow from 0.9 to 0.50 m over each ramp, which cross-falls 3° to the centre. A 10 mm rubber catch ring circles the flush cup. About 2.2–2.35 m/s from the tee.
holes.build: Graded ribs under a flexi-ply skin, a solid plateau for the cup sleeve, tapered rails. Two bridge-tower flats on posts outside the rails, sandbagged, crossbeams at 2.1 m or more, with festoon "cables" at least 2.4 m up. Plank-printed roadway, yellow LED.
holes.miss: Every miss returns by gravity to an end, so nothing stops out of reach. A ball that crosses is played by its owner from the end it reached, after the other player.
holes.risks: Smashes ("no backswing above the knee"); simultaneous clashes upsetting kids; floor level under the cross-fall; tower openings at head height.
holes.surface: Plank-printed roadway over the hump; its ends meet Liberty's harbour carpet.
holes.prop: Graded ribs under a flexi-ply skin, a solid plateau for the cup sleeve, tapered rails. Two bridge-tower flats on posts outside the rails, sandbagged, crossbeams at 2.1 m or more, with festoon "cables" at least 2.4 m up. Plank-printed roadway, yellow LED.
holes.robust: Every miss returns by gravity to an end, so nothing stops out of reach. A ball that crosses is played by its owner from the end it reached, after the other player.

holes.name: Liberty Island
holes.play: Putt along the blue harbour at a breaking wave in the corner. The ball rides round it 90° toward Liberty Island; with pace it climbs the shore and runs at the cup in the star-shaped pedestal. Too soft slides back to the wave foot; too hard lands deep.
holes.mech: Leg A: a 3.0 × 0.9 m harbour. The corner is a conical banked face curved at about R 1.0 m in plan, 400 mm high with a 50 mm curl lip and cheeks closed to the rails, so the ball rides round at any speed. Leg B: a 2.2 × 1.4 m island 75 mm up a 1:5 shore; cup 1.2 m past the crest.
holes.build: Tapered radial ribs at 150 mm or less under a flexi-ply skin, closed back, padded curl nosing, foot seam 1 mm or less; island deck; the 2.6 m statue (drawn from the original 1886 statue) with a battery flame on a pedestal of at least 30 kg outside the rail. Wave paint, harbour skyline, teal LED.
holes.miss: Weak balls roll back to the wave foot within 0.6 m of a rail. The bank is closed at both cheeks, so nothing leaves the hole.
holes.risks: Kids treating the wave as a skate ramp ("no climbing" pictogram, marshal brief); pace (lever: cup 0.3 m nearer the crest). The full-width rig on 3 Dec must send at least 70% to the island, or it falls back to a flat chamfer bank.
holes.surface: Blue harbour carpet with a painted breaking wave; green island with a painted star.
holes.prop: Tapered radial ribs at 150 mm or less under a flexi-ply skin, closed back, padded curl nosing, foot seam 1 mm or less; island deck; the 2.6 m statue (drawn from the original 1886 statue) with a battery flame on a pedestal of at least 30 kg outside the rail. Wave paint, harbour skyline, teal LED.
holes.robust: Weak balls roll back to the wave foot within 0.6 m of a rail. The bank is closed at both cheeks, so nothing leaves the hole.

holes.name: Central Park Loop
holes.play: Midtown's teaching hole. A park path zig-zags twice; each curved outer rail carries a well-paced ball round, under a stone arch and onto a flat lawn to the cup in a fountain. Sign line: "the rail is your friend".
holes.mech: Path 0.9 m; legs 1.8, 1.2 and 2.2 m. Outer corners curved R 0.9 m with a hard, low-friction face; inner corners rounded and filled. The lawn stays flat: the factory deck gives the cup its depth. Expect 25–30% speed loss per corner, so an ace is doubtful.
holes.build: Each curve is five stacked plywood arcs, the top one forming the cap, screwed to plates every 300 mm: no spring-back, no free ends. Two borrowed Christmas trees (bases 0.9 m or less) with fairy lights in the Z's pockets, the old bike wheels outside the rails, benches, lamp posts, arch, fountain, blue LED. A painted park-wall cut-out faces Gridlock.
holes.miss: A soft ball stops within 0.45 m of a rail; a hard one rides the curve. Every resting spot is in reach.
holes.risks: Scrub on the curves (measure the loss on the 3 Dec corner rig); tree bases breaking clearances; the course's slowest hole at up to 2.7 min (lever: tee at leg 2).
holes.surface: Green carpet grass path and a flat lawn round the fountain cup.
holes.prop: Each curve is five stacked plywood arcs, the top one forming the cap, screwed to plates every 300 mm: no spring-back, no free ends. Two borrowed Christmas trees (bases 0.9 m or less) with fairy lights in the Z's pockets, the old bike wheels outside the rails, benches, lamp posts, arch, fountain, blue LED. A painted park-wall cut-out faces Gridlock.
holes.robust: A soft ball stops within 0.45 m of a rail; a hard one rides the curve. Every resting spot is in reach.

holes.name: Gridlock
holes.play: Putt through a jam of eight cabs on Fifth Avenue; bold players thread one of two avenues, and two angled cabs bank toward a manhole-cover cup on a zebra crossing. The kids-against-adults equaliser.
holes.mech: Lane 5.0 × 1.8 m. Cabs 360 × 170 × 140 mm in two staggered rows of 3 (avenues about 0.30–0.35 m) plus two at 30°. Every gap at least 0.27 m or closed, and the acute pockets by the angled cabs filled. The zebra crossing is printed flat, with the manhole-cover cup on it.
holes.build: Charcoal needle-punch lane, yellow lines and a printed zebra crossing; cab blocks screwed down from below; invented "CAB 1159" livery, cones painted on the rails, purple LED. Hole 3's subway kiosk stands on its sidewalk.
holes.miss: Every resting spot is within 0.9 m of a rail, and no pocket can trap a ball where a putter can't reach.
holes.risks: Acute V pockets by the angled cabs (fill them); chaos strokes slowing the hole (lever: open an avenue).
holes.surface: Charcoal "asphalt" needle-punch, yellow lane lines, a printed zebra crossing.
holes.prop: Charcoal needle-punch lane, yellow lines and a printed zebra crossing; cab blocks screwed down from below; invented "CAB 1159" livery, cones painted on the rails, purple LED. Hole 3's subway kiosk stands on its sidewalk.
holes.robust: Every resting spot is within 0.9 m of a rail, and no pocket can trap a ball where a putter can't reach.

holes.name: The Subway
holes.sign: Stand Clear of the Closing Doors
holes.play: Putt up the station steps. Funnel rails steer the ball into one of three tiled portals (left Express, centre Local, right Shuttle). It vanishes, races round a hairpin under a clear lid and shoots out on the opposite side heading back toward you, with the Express exit on the cup line. Walk round and putt out.
holes.mech: A 1:6 ramp climbs about 245 mm to a 0.5 m platform falling 1:12 to three 110 mm portals. 1:4 lead-ins drop each ball into a loop floor tilted 5–6°: hairpins R 0.30, 0.44 and 0.58 m under a clear lid. Carpeted bevels step down to the return green; cup 1.2 m out on the Express line.
holes.build: Ramp and platform; a loop box with a tilted plane floor, shaped lead-ins and walls of stacked plywood arcs (CNC-cut); a 4 mm polycarbonate lid with 60 mm headroom and four thumbscrews; return green; a 0.4 m island box. White-tile portal wall with invented line symbols (star, ring, diamond), ice-blue LED. Its 1.6 m kiosk with globe lamps stands on Gridlock's sidewalk.
holes.miss: Too soft rolls back down the ramp to the tee; every channel falls, so no ball can stall inside, and the lid lifts off in under 20 s if one ever does.
holes.risks: Loop stall is the course's main physics unknown (lever: a bigger entry drop, not a bigger radius); the ramp needs about 2.5 m/s, hard for small kids (junior tee at the ramp foot; after two roll-backs, place it on the platform for +1); polycarbonate fire rating. Built first, as the 4 Dec prototype.
holes.surface: Carpet grass steps, platform and return green; white subway-tile portal wall; clear lid over the loops.
holes.prop: Ramp and platform; a loop box with a tilted plane floor, shaped lead-ins and walls of stacked plywood arcs (CNC-cut); a 4 mm polycarbonate lid with 60 mm headroom and four thumbscrews; return green; a 0.4 m island box. White-tile portal wall with invented line symbols (star, ring, diamond), ice-blue LED. Its 1.6 m kiosk with globe lamps stands on Gridlock's sidewalk.
holes.robust: Too soft rolls back down the ramp to the tee; every channel falls, so no ball can stall inside, and the lid lifts off in under 20 s if one ever does.

holes.name: Grand Central Whispering Gallery
holes.play: Tee at the brass whisper spot. A round information booth blocks the straight line to the cup at the other spot, under the big clock. The sign: "Aim anywhere off the wall. Every bounce is the same distance." The game is the weight.
holes.mech: Ellipse a = 1.40, b = 0.95 m, so each focus is 1.03 m from the centre: tee at one, cup at the other, and every wall path is 2.80 m. The Ø0.40 × 0.35 m booth blocks shots within about ±12° of the straight line. One flat deck levelled to ±2 mm. About 1.9–2.4 m/s from the tee.
holes.build: A deck in three pieces (seams over 300 mm from the spots), a three-lamination flexi-ply rail with a hard lacquered face (no EVA), the ballasted booth with four clock faces, and the Ø1 m clock at 11:59 on a 30 kg braced post behind the cup. Teal star field, brass spots, amber LED.
holes.miss: The ellipse returns every ball; nothing is ever more than 0.95 m from the rail.
holes.risks: Real rebounds (the 3 Dec rig with the real face decides; the octagon fallback is drawn); deck level; laminations opening. If scatter fails, a shallow 1.5–2° dish round the cup.
holes.clock: The big clock at 11:59, facing hole 1's 2027.
holes.surface: Green carpet grass ellipse, brass whisper spots, teal star-field backdrop.
holes.prop: A deck in three pieces (seams over 300 mm from the spots), a three-lamination flexi-ply rail with a hard lacquered face (no EVA), the ballasted booth with four clock faces, and the Ø1 m clock at 11:59 on a 30 kg braced post behind the cup. Teal star field, brass spots, amber LED.
holes.robust: The ellipse returns every ball; nothing is ever more than 0.95 m from the rail.

holes.name: Times Square
holes.play: The finale. Putt up the red steps; too soft rolls back for another try. Over the crest the ball rattles down a lit peg board under a clear cover into a slot marked 3, 2, 1, 2, 3; the centre is DROP and the 2027 neon flashes. Score is roll-backs plus the slot number. Every ball rolls out to a tray and goes back to the hub.
holes.mech: Lane 1.0 m with 0.8 m of flat from the tee. A 1:6 ramp, 1.2 m long, climbs 200 mm; the 0.3 m crest tilts 3° toward the board. Board 0.80 × 0.80 m at 12° with about 115 pegs under a clear cover; five 130 mm slots run out to an open tray. About 2.3 m/s from the tee.
holes.build: Ribbed ramp with a flexi skin, a jig-drilled peg board under a 4 mm polycarbonate cover, slots and a carpet-lined floor tray. A 2.8 m tower with 2027 neon and a borrowed mirror ball (optional battery spinner, decor only), braced and ballasted at 60 kg or more; two billboards with invented brands facing the party floor; magenta LED.
holes.miss: A weak putt rolls back to the tee; nothing can stop on the covered board or the tilted crest; no ball is kept.
holes.risks: Kids cresting (junior tee at the ramp foot, place rule); peg jams (200-drop rig); tower ballast; fire rating; rolling it aside if golf closes before midnight. Say "countdown ball", never the trademarked name.
holes.surface: Red-step ramp, lit peg board under a clear cover, carpet-lined tray.
holes.prop: Ribbed ramp with a flexi skin, a jig-drilled peg board under a 4 mm polycarbonate cover, slots and a carpet-lined floor tray. A 2.8 m tower with 2027 neon and a borrowed mirror ball (optional battery spinner, decor only), braced and ballasted at 60 kg or more; two billboards with invented brands facing the party floor; magenta LED.
holes.robust: A weak putt rolls back to the tee; nothing can stop on the covered board or the tilted crest; no ball is kept.
